claims.text: The disputed SGD 5.00 is not in the rider's hands now: EV-FARE-05067 records the fee charged at 09:30:14 and refunded the same day, with payment_status = REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd = 5.00, and the trip record's own event log shows the money was withheld from the driver pending this review. Under POL-GEN-03 the five ruling values are party-relative, and FULL_REFUND and PARTIAL_REFUND are defined against the FILER - here the driver, not the rider. The rider's win on this filing is therefore that the present state stands, which is exactly what NO_ACTION means; any ruling that moves money on this record moves it toward the driver.

The record tells us nothing about where the rider was. EV-GPS-05067 carries an empty rider_track, and its arrival check measures only the driver's own fixes against the recorded pickup coordinate; no artifact in the package shows the rider away from the pickup, unable to board, or refusing to board. A cancellation 'as a rider no-show' under POL-NS-21 turns on precisely that fact, and POL-GEN-26 requires that where a fact a rule needs cannot be established on the evidence, the case goes to a human reviewer and no outcome is inferred from the gap - its second sentence forbids exactly the inference the driver's filing asks for.

Even the driver's arrival is proved only against a bare coordinate, not against this rider's block. The pickup carries venue_id = null in EV-TRIP-05067, and nothing in the record - no venue_id, and no party statement in the chat log - identifies that coordinate as the rider's block or entrance. POL-NS-21's arrival test in EV-GPS-05067 asks only whether the driver's fixes sat within the STANDARD zone radius of 50 m of that coordinate (nearest fix 1.81 m), and the arrival marker it corroborates is itself GPS-derived ('Auto-arrival from driver GPS', EV-TRIP-05067), so the trace is corroborating a marker drawn from the same device's own trace. The single question that matters - was the driver where this rider was waiting - is not settled by this record.

Any AI ruling on this dispute must be reached at 0.95 confidence. The rider's profile carries rider_profile.fraud_flags = 3 (EV-RPROF-05067), and POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 wherever a party's profile carries a fraud flag, whatever the dispute value; POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling expressly subject to that bar. The driver's filing asks the platform to undo an interim reversal and take SGD 5.00 back from a rider who is not now carrying it, on a record that resolves only the driver's half of the encounter. At a 0.95 bar the AI should not re-charge her, and the case belongs to a human reviewer.

The one rider-favouring test on this policy is POL-NS-24, which measures the driver's lateness from the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes - and this trip has no scheduled time at all: driver_deadline.deadline is null in EV-TRIP-05067, for the stated reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. The test that could have answered this case in the rider's favour therefore cannot be applied on this record, and that unresolved question goes to a human reviewer rather than to a re-charge.

The record has no source outside the platform's own telemetry and the driver's own device: the only third-party artifact for this trip, the LTA traffic advisory, is absent. EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is MISSING, its issue codes are MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its weight is 0.0 - I disclose that impairment rather than present it as clean evidence. POL-GEN-02 makes the completeness of the evidence part of the confidence a ruling is held to, and on a filing that would move SGD 5.00 to the driver, the absence of any independent source tells against finality and against re-charging the rider on this record.

I concede the contact obligation and do not build on it: EV-CHAT-05067 shows three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and EV-TRIP-05067 shows two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), every one of them before cancelled_at at 09:30:10, which is why the derived contact_before_cancel block records obligation_met = true. POL-NS-23 is satisfied on this record. The rider's case does not rest on it; it rests on the facts this record leaves unresolved - where the rider was, and whether the charge should be taken from her a second time.

The trip record's arrival event at 09:21:45 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix to the recorded pickup point is 1.81 m away (fix index 13, ts 09:22:20, reported accuracy 6 m), far inside the 50 m arrival radius that the category's arrival test sets for a STANDARD pickup zone, and after that fix the trace shows the vehicle held at 0 kph from 09:21:50 through the last fix at 09:29:50 (EV-GPS-05067). The arrival test is therefore satisfied, and because this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled_at, the free wait runs from arrived_at under POL-NS-21.

The driver waited out the full free wait and then some. Arrival at 09:21:45 with a 300-second free wait gives an expiry of 09:26:45 (EV-TRIP-05067, free_wait.ends_at, free_wait_sec 300 under POL-NS-21); the driver cancelled at 09:30:10, which is 505 seconds after arrival — 205 seconds past the expiry (EV-TRIP-05067, free_wait.seconds_from_start_to_cancel and cancelled_after_free_wait true). The condition POL-NS-21 attaches to a lawful no-show cancellation was met, so the fee was properly chargeable under POL-NS-22.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met in full. Before cancelled_at 09:30:10 the driver sent three in-app chat messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40 per EV-CHAT-05067) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, rang 30 s unanswered; 09:27:20, rang 25 s unanswered per EV-TRIP-05067). Both limbs — at least one message AND at least one in-app call, each before cancellation — are satisfied, so the FULL_REFUND consequence POL-NS-23 attaches to a missing contact step is not engaged and the fee must not be voided on that ground.

The rider was not left guessing. The chat log records delivery and a read receipt for every driver message — read at 09:22:42, 09:25:37 and 09:29:09 — including the final notice 'Going to cancel in 1 min if no reply ya', read 61 seconds before the 09:30:10 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05067, read_at fields; message_count 3 consistent with trip_record.chat_message_count). The rider therefore had actual notice of the driver's presence and of the impending cancellation, which is precisely the protective purpose POL-NS-23 serves.

The rider's counter-account — 'The driver never came to my block. I was downstairs waiting.' — is contradicted by the driver-device trace, which places the device within 1.81 m of the recorded pickup point and stationary there (0 kph across consecutive fixes) for over eight minutes before cancellation (EV-GPS-05067). Nor is there any rider-side location evidence to support the rider's account: the trace's rider_track is empty, so nothing on the record shows the rider at the pickup point at all. POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) is not engaged: the driver did arrive, the trip was on-demand with no scheduled time, and no driver lateness can be fixed against him.

The amount is exactly the policy amount: 5.00 SGD was charged on 09:30:14 and fee_matches_policy is true, with policy_fee_sgd 5.00 and driver_compensation_if_upheld_sgd 5.00 under POL-NS-22 (EV-FARE-05067). The remedy the driver seeks is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD. This matters because of the money's present position: the ledger shows an interim reversal at 10:46:10 that refunded the 5.00 to the rider and withheld it from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.0). Under POL-GEN-03 NO_ACTION preserves that present state, which would leave the driver unpaid for a no-show he lawfully established; only DRIVER_COMPENSATION moves the 5.00 to the driver, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00.

Nothing here needs a human. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and so carries no fact at all. No rule in the no-show category requires traffic data, and every fact POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22 and POL-NS-23 need — arrival, the free wait, the fee charged, the messages and the calls before cancellation — is established on artifacts assessed COMPLETE at full weight. There is no open question of the kind POL-GEN-26 sends to a reviewer, and the absence of a third-party advisory is not evidence of anything.

The record can bear the confidence this case requires. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3, which under POL-GEN-22 raises the required confidence to 0.95; rider_profile.fraud_flags is one of the two profile fields POL-GEN-01 permits to be cited, and only for this test — it does not decide the trip. The artifacts that carry the deciding facts (TRIP_RECORD, GPS_TRACE, CHAT_LOG and FARE_BREAKDOWN) are each COMPLETE with weight_multiplier 1.0 and are mutually consistent — the trace's arrival matches the record's arrived_at, message_count matches the trip record, and the ledger reconciles to total_charged 5.00 — so the driver's case can be found at the 0.95 confidence POL-GEN-22 demands.

ruling.explanation:
Driver — the SGD 5.00 no-show fee was properly chargeable, and the record shows you are owed it. Rider — the record does not support the account you filed.

What the record shows. This was an on-demand trip booked at 09:15:00, so under POL-NS-21 the free wait runs from the driver's arrival, not from a schedule. The arrival marker at 09:21:45 (EV-TRIP-05067) is corroborated by the driver-device trace (EV-GPS-05067): the nearest fix sits 1.81 m from the recorded pickup coordinate with a reported accuracy of 6 m, far inside the 50 m radius the STANDARD-zone arrival test sets, and the trace then holds at 0 km/h from 09:21:50 through the last fix at 09:29:50. The 300-second free wait therefore expired at 09:26:45, and the driver cancelled at 09:30:10 — 505 seconds after arrival, 205 seconds past expiry. POL-NS-21 is satisfied.

Contact. Before cancelling, the driver sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40 — EV-CHAT-05067) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, rang 30 s unanswered; 09:27:20, rang 25 s unanswered — EV-TRIP-05067). POL-NS-23 requires at least one message AND at least one call before cancelled_at, and both limbs are met, so the fee is not voided on that ground. Rider — the read receipts show you read all three messages, including the final 'Going to cancel in 1 min' notice at 09:29:09.

Rider's account. Your statement that the driver 'never came to my block' is contradicted by the trace, which places the driver's device at the recorded pickup coordinate and stationary there for over eight minutes. There is no rider-side location record at all (rider_track is empty), so nothing on the record corroborates your account, and I do not accept it.

Rider's escalation arguments. POL-GEN-26 does not apply. Every fact the governing rules need is established: the arrival test reads the driver's own position; the free-wait test reads arrival and cancellation times; the contact test reads the messages and calls; the fee test reads the ledger. Where you were standing is not a fact any of these clauses makes its test, so its absence opens no question. The empty rider_track and the absent LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05067-01, weight 0.0, MISSING_ARTIFACT) carry no fact any rule requires, and the absence of a traffic advisory is not itself evidence of anything. POL-NS-24 does not assist you either: it refunds a rider where the driver failed to arrive by the deadline, whereas here the driver arrived about seven minutes after booking and waited — there is no lateness to fix. Your POL-GEN-03 point is right that the outcomes are party-relative and that money on this record moves only toward the driver; that is exactly what happens, because the driver's claim is supported.

Money. The fee charged is exactly the policy amount — SGD 5.00 (EV-FARE-05067, fee_matches_policy true). The interim reversal at 10:46:10 returned that SGD 5.00 to the rider and withheld it from the driver. Because the fee stands, POL-NS-22 moves the SGD 5.00 to the driver: the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both SGD 5.00.

Confidence. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3 (EV-RPROF-05067), so POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling subject to that bar. The artifacts that carry the deciding facts — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — are each COMPLETE at weight 1.0, and they are mutually consistent, so the bar is met at 0.95.

No referral fires. The fee is exactly SGD 5.00, so POL-NS-22's fee-amount check does not trigger; the driver did arrive and did attempt contact, so no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit arises; and the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d count, including this trip, is 2 — below the POL-NS-25 threshold of 3.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties: this is the no-show charge on trip TRP-05067, decided on the record under the Ryde Dispute Resolution Policy v2.1.

The driver's no-show cancellation is upheld. The driver arrived at the recorded pickup at 09:21:45 and the driver-device GPS trace corroborates it — the nearest fix sits 1.81 m from the pickup coordinate, well inside the 50 m arrival radius for a STANDARD zone (EV-GPS-05067, EV-TRIP-05067). Because this was an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, the 300-second free wait under POL-NS-21 runs from arrival and expired at 09:26:45; the driver cancelled at 09:30:10, 505 seconds after arrival and about 205 seconds past expiry, with the vehicle stationary at the pickup throughout. The contact obligation under POL-NS-23 (v2.1 2.3) is met: three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40, EV-CHAT-05067) and two in-app calls (09:24:10 ringing 30 s unanswered; 09:27:20 ringing 25 s unanswered, EV-TRIP-05067), every one before cancellation; the log shows the rider read each message. The 5.00 SGD charged matches the policy fee (EV-FARE-05067, fee_matches_policy true, policy fee 5.00). Under POL-NS-22 the fee therefore stands and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD, with amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both 5.00 (the same figure, the money the ruling moves). Because an interim reversal already refunded the 5.00 to the rider and withheld it from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED), this ruling moves that 5.00 back to the driver.

The rider's points are considered. It is true the rider-side track is empty and no artifact places the rider at the pickup, and true that the arrival is proved against the recorded coordinate rather than a named entrance (venue_id is null). But the rider's location is not the test any clause sets for a no-show charge: POL-NS-21's test is the driver's arrival plus the free wait, and POL-NS-23's test is the messages and calls, and the record establishes both. The empty rider-side track therefore creates no open question and POL-GEN-26 does not apply. POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) does not engage: the driver arrived and waited, so no failure to arrive can be found, and there is no scheduled deadline to fix on an on-demand trip; the FULL_REFUND that POL-NS-23 and POL-NS-24 attach to their conditions does not arise. The absent LTA traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05067-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact and no rule requires traffic data, so its absence does not defeat the ruling (POL-GEN-02).

On what governs the confidence: the rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3 (EV-RPROF-05067), and POL-GEN-22 (v2.1 6.3), with POL-NS-26, raises the confidence an AI ruling needs to 0.95. The artifacts that carry the deciding facts — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger — are all COMPLETE at weight 1.0 and are mutually consistent, so the confidence cap is 1.0 and the 0.95 bar is met. No referral is produced: POL-NS-22's fee-amount check is not triggered (the amount charged is exactly 5.00), POL-NS-24's goodwill credit does not apply (contact was attempted), and POL-NS-25's repeat no-show flag does not apply (the 30-day count, counting this trip, is 2, below 3).

ruling.explanation:
Ruling on TRP-05067 (case 5067), for driver D-79082 and rider R-18402. The driver cancelled at 09:30:10 as a rider no-show and a 5.00 SGD fee was charged; the platform later reversed it (event log 10:46:10), so the 5.00 SGD currently sits with the rider. The fee stands: the 5.00 SGD moves to the driver.

Arrival (POL-NS-21 and the category arrival test). The trip record's auto-arrival at 09:21:45 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix sits 1.81 m from the recorded pickup coordinate with a reported accuracy of 6 m, far inside the 50 m radius this category sets for a STANDARD zone (EV-GPS-05067, arrival_check; corroborated true). That is the test POL-NS-21 and the category define for arrival, and it is met. The rider's account that the driver 'never came to my block' is contradicted by the trace, and there is no rider-side location evidence on the record (rider_track is empty). That the pickup coordinate carries no venue_id does not undo the test: it is the coordinate the rider booked the pickup from, and the policy's arrival test is measured against it.

Free wait and fee (POL-NS-21, POL-NS-22). This was an on-demand booking with no scheduled time, so the 300-second free wait ran from arrival at 09:21:45 and expired at 09:26:45 (EV-TRIP-05067, free_wait: starts_from 'arrived_at', ends_at 09:26:45). The driver cancelled at 09:30:10, 505 seconds after arrival — past the free wait (cancelled_after_free_wait true). The condition POL-NS-21 attaches to a lawful no-show cancellation was therefore met, and the fee was properly chargeable (EV-FARE-05067: fee_matches_policy true, policy_fee_sgd 5.00, fee_charged_sgd 5.00).

Contact obligation (POL-NS-23). Before cancelled_at 09:30:10 the driver sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40, all read; EV-CHAT-05067) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10 ringing 30 s unanswered; 09:27:20 ringing 25 s unanswered; EV-TRIP-05067). Both limbs — at least one message and at least one call before cancellation — are satisfied (obligation_met true), and the rider's own case concedes this. The FULL_REFUND consequence POL-NS-23 attaches to a missing contact step is not engaged.

POL-NS-24 and POL-GEN-26 (the rider's escalation argument). POL-NS-24 measures lateness from the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes; this on-demand trip has no scheduled time (driver_deadline.deadline null, reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'), so that lateness test cannot fix a deadline and gives the rider no refund. It also does not send the case to a human reviewer. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule of this version actually needs cannot be established on the evidence, and the facts the no-show rules need — when the driver arrived (09:21:45, corroborated) and whether he messaged and called before cancelling (he did) — are both established at full weight. The absence of the LTA traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-05067-01, MISSING, weight 0.0) carries no fact and no rule in this category requires traffic data, so it too raises no open question.

Confidence (POL-GEN-22, POL-NS-26). The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 3, so the ruling is held to a confidence of 0.95 whatever the dispute value, and POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling subject to that bar. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 and are mutually consistent (trace arrival matches the record's arrived_at; message_count matches; the ledger reconciles to total_charged 5.00), so the cap is 1.0 and the 0.95 bar is reached. The other profile fields (rating, history, prior flags) are context only under POL-GEN-01 and decide nothing; fraud_flags is cited only for this confidence test and does not decide the trip.

Repeat no-show flag (POL-NS-25). The rider's no_show_cancellations_30d is 1; counting this trip if its fee stands gives 2, below the threshold of 3, so no referral is raised.

Outcome. Under POL-GEN-03 the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, and amount_sgd and driver_compensation_sgd both carry the same 5.00 SGD — the money this ruling moves to the driver, not a second payment and not a refund to the filing party. It is the 5.00 SGD presently refunded to the rider, restored to the driver for a no-show he lawfully established. No clause produces a referral on these figures: the fee charged equals the 5.00 SGD policy fee (POL-NS-22), no POL-NS-24 goodwill credit is due, and the POL-NS-25 threshold is not met.

ruling.explanation:
To the driver and the rider. Trip TRP-05067 was an on-demand Ryde X booking from Block 680, Choa Chu Kang Crescent. The driver cancelled at 09:30:10 as a rider no-show, a 5.00 SGD fee was charged at 09:30:14, and at 10:46:10 that 5.00 SGD was returned to the rider and withheld from the driver pending this review. On this record the fee stands, so the 5.00 SGD moves back to the driver.

WHY THE FEE STANDS. (1) POL-NS-21 (free wait): the trip record's arrival event at 09:21:45 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace — the nearest fix is 1.81 m from the recorded pickup coordinate (fix 13, 09:22:20, reported accuracy 6 m), well inside the 50 m radius for a STANDARD pickup — and the trace holds the vehicle at 0 kph from 09:21:50 through 09:29:50. This being an on-demand trip with no scheduled time, the 300 s free wait ran from arrival to 09:26:45; the driver cancelled at 09:30:10, 505 s after arrival, 205 s past expiry. (2) POL-NS-23 (contact): before cancelling the driver sent three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10 and 09:27:20, both unanswered), so both limbs are met and the FULL_REFUND that clause attaches to a missed step is not engaged. (3) POL-NS-22 (the fee): 5.00 SGD was charged and fee_matches_policy is true; where the fee stands the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION with both money fields equal to the fee charged, and under POL-GEN-03 amount_sgd carries the same figure as driver_compensation_sgd (5.00 SGD).

THE RIDER'S POINTS. Your account that the driver never came to your block is contradicted by the driver-device trace and nothing on the record supports it — rider_track is empty, so there is no rider-side location evidence at all. POL-GEN-26 escalates only where a fact a rule must have cannot be established; the facts the no-show rules need (arrival, the free wait, the messages and the calls before cancellation) are all established at full weight. POL-NS-24 (driver no-show) is the rider's remedy and is engaged only where the rider cancels because the driver failed to arrive; you did not cancel and the driver did arrive, so that clause is not in play, and its on-demand deadline gap does not leave a fact this ruling needs because POL-NS-21 supplies the on-demand treatment. The 10:46:10 reversal was a holding step pending review, not a final outcome, so the party-relative reading of POL-GEN-03 does not freeze it once the fee is found to stand. The absent LTA advisory (EV-ADVIS-05067-01, MISSING_ARTIFACT, weight 0.0) carries no fact, and no rule here requires traffic data, so it neither lowers confidence nor opens a question.

The driver's evidence points — arrival corroboration, the free wait, the contact steps, the 5.00 SGD amount, and that the record can bear the required confidence — are accepted; the contact obligation is common ground.

CONFIDENCE. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags 3, so POL-GEN-22 (with POL-NS-26) requires 0.95. The artifacts carrying the deciding facts — trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown — are each COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap is 1.0 and this ruling issues at 0.95.

NO REFERRAL APPLIES: the fee charged is exactly the 5.00 SGD policy fee (POL-NS-22 referral not triggered); the driver attempted contact, so the POL-NS-24 goodwill credit does not arise; and the rider's no_show_cancellations_30d of 1, counting this trip, reaches 2, below the POL-NS-25 threshold of 3.

ledger.claim: The disputed SGD 5.00 is not in the rider's hands now: EV-FARE-05067 records the fee charged at 09:30:14 and refunded the same day, with payment_status = REFUNDED and refund_issued_sgd = 5.00, and the trip record's own event log shows the money was withheld from the driver pending this review. Under POL-GEN-03 the five ruling values are party-relative, and FULL_REFUND and PARTIAL_REFUND are defined against the FILER - here the driver, not the rider. The rider's win on this filing is therefore that the present state stands, which is exactly what NO_ACTION means; any ruling that moves money on this record moves it toward the driver.

The record tells us nothing about where the rider was. EV-GPS-05067 carries an empty rider_track, and its arrival check measures only the driver's own fixes against the recorded pickup coordinate; no artifact in the package shows the rider away from the pickup, unable to board, or refusing to board. A cancellation 'as a rider no-show' under POL-NS-21 turns on precisely that fact, and POL-GEN-26 requires that where a fact a rule needs cannot be established on the evidence, the case goes to a human reviewer and no outcome is inferred from the gap - its second sentence forbids exactly the inference the driver's filing asks for.

Even the driver's arrival is proved only against a bare coordinate, not against this rider's block. The pickup carries venue_id = null in EV-TRIP-05067, and nothing in the record - no venue_id, and no party statement in the chat log - identifies that coordinate as the rider's block or entrance. POL-NS-21's arrival test in EV-GPS-05067 asks only whether the driver's fixes sat within the STANDARD zone radius of 50 m of that coordinate (nearest fix 1.81 m), and the arrival marker it corroborates is itself GPS-derived ('Auto-arrival from driver GPS', EV-TRIP-05067), so the trace is corroborating a marker drawn from the same device's own trace. The single question that matters - was the driver where this rider was waiting - is not settled by this record.

Any AI ruling on this dispute must be reached at 0.95 confidence. The rider's profile carries rider_profile.fraud_flags = 3 (EV-RPROF-05067), and POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 wherever a party's profile carries a fraud flag, whatever the dispute value; POL-NS-26 makes the no-show ruling expressly subject to that bar. The driver's filing asks the platform to undo an interim reversal and take SGD 5.00 back from a rider who is not now carrying it, on a record that resolves only the driver's half of the encounter. At a 0.95 bar the AI should not re-charge her, and the case belongs to a human reviewer.

The one rider-favouring test on this policy is POL-NS-24, which measures the driver's lateness from the scheduled pickup time plus 5 minutes - and this trip has no scheduled time at all: driver_deadline.deadline is null in EV-TRIP-05067, for the stated reason 'on-demand trip: no scheduled time'. POL-NS-24's own note directs that where the record carries no scheduled time and the deadline cannot be fixed, POL-GEN-26 applies. The test that could have answered this case in the rider's favour therefore cannot be applied on this record, and that unresolved question goes to a human reviewer rather than to a re-charge.

The record has no source outside the platform's own telemetry and the driver's own device: the only third-party artifact for this trip, the LTA traffic advisory, is absent. EV-ADVIS-05067-01 is MISSING, its issue codes are MISSING_ARTIFACT, and its weight is 0.0 - I disclose that impairment rather than present it as clean evidence. POL-GEN-02 makes the completeness of the evidence part of the confidence a ruling is held to, and on a filing that would move SGD 5.00 to the driver, the absence of any independent source tells against finality and against re-charging the rider on this record.

I concede the contact obligation and do not build on it: EV-CHAT-05067 shows three in-app messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40) and EV-TRIP-05067 shows two in-app calls (09:24:10, 09:27:20), every one of them before cancelled_at at 09:30:10, which is why the derived contact_before_cancel block records obligation_met = true. POL-NS-23 is satisfied on this record. The rider's case does not rest on it; it rests on the facts this record leaves unresolved - where the rider was, and whether the charge should be taken from her a second time.

The trip record's arrival event at 09:21:45 is corroborated by the driver-device GPS trace: the nearest fix to the recorded pickup point is 1.81 m away (fix index 13, ts 09:22:20, reported accuracy 6 m), far inside the 50 m arrival radius that the category's arrival test sets for a STANDARD pickup zone, and after that fix the trace shows the vehicle held at 0 kph from 09:21:50 through the last fix at 09:29:50 (EV-GPS-05067). The arrival test is therefore satisfied, and because this is an on-demand trip with no scheduled_at, the free wait runs from arrived_at under POL-NS-21.

The driver waited out the full free wait and then some. Arrival at 09:21:45 with a 300-second free wait gives an expiry of 09:26:45 (EV-TRIP-05067, free_wait.ends_at, free_wait_sec 300 under POL-NS-21); the driver cancelled at 09:30:10, which is 505 seconds after arrival — 205 seconds past the expiry (EV-TRIP-05067, free_wait.seconds_from_start_to_cancel and cancelled_after_free_wait true). The condition POL-NS-21 attaches to a lawful no-show cancellation was met, so the fee was properly chargeable under POL-NS-22.

POL-NS-23's contact obligation is met in full. Before cancelled_at 09:30:10 the driver sent three in-app chat messages (09:22:00, 09:25:30, 09:28:40 per EV-CHAT-05067) and placed two in-app calls (09:24:10, rang 30 s unanswered; 09:27:20, rang 25 s unanswered per EV-TRIP-05067). Both limbs — at least one message AND at least one in-app call, each before cancellation — are satisfied, so the FULL_REFUND consequence POL-NS-23 attaches to a missing contact step is not engaged and the fee must not be voided on that ground.

The rider was not left guessing. The chat log records delivery and a read receipt for every driver message — read at 09:22:42, 09:25:37 and 09:29:09 — including the final notice 'Going to cancel in 1 min if no reply ya', read 61 seconds before the 09:30:10 cancellation (EV-CHAT-05067, read_at fields; message_count 3 consistent with trip_record.chat_message_count). The rider therefore had actual notice of the driver's presence and of the impending cancellation, which is precisely the protective purpose POL-NS-23 serves.

The rider's counter-account — 'The driver never came to my block. The remedy the driver seeks is therefore DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 5.00 SGD. This matters because of the money's present position: the ledger shows an interim reversal at 10:46:10 that refunded the 5.00 to the rider and withheld it from the driver (payment_status REFUNDED, refund_issued_sgd 5.0).
